options: A big building where electricity is made
powerplant.hint: The answer is "A big building where electricity is made". A power plant is a facility where electricity is generated.

powerplant.q: What does a power plant make?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "Electricity". Power plants are built to generate electricity.

options: Power plants are tiny devices you hold
Power plants store sunlight in jars
powerplant.hint: The answer is "Power plants generate electricity". A power plant is a big facility that makes electricity.

powerplant.q: Fill in the blank: A power plant is a facility where electricity is ____.
powerplant.hint: The answer is "generated". Generated means made, and power plants make electricity.

powerplant.q: Which term means "a big building where electricity is made"?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "Power plant". That is the meaning of power plant.

powerplant.q: Which of these is a power plant?
options: A building where turbines make electricity for a city
A flower pot on a window
powerplant.hint: The answer is "A building where turbines make electricity for a city". Only that building makes electricity for many people.

powerplant.q: Which of these is NOT a power plant?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "A flashlight". A flashlight is a small device, not a big facility that makes electricity.

powerplant.q: Which item would you find inside a power plant?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "A huge generator". Power plants use giant generators to make electricity.

powerplant.q: Which group lists only places that make electricity?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "Wind farm, solar plant, dam". Each of those places generates electricity.

powerplant.q: Which is a power plant that uses moving water?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "A hydroelectric dam". A hydroelectric dam uses moving water to make electricity.

powerplant.q: The lights in your classroom are on. Where was that electricity most likely made?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "At a power plant". Electricity is made at a power plant and sent to buildings.

powerplant.q: A town is growing and needs more electricity. What could it build?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "A new power plant". A power plant is the place that makes electricity.

powerplant.q: A storm shuts down the town's only power plant. What might happen?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "Homes may lose electricity". If the power plant stops, electricity stops being made for homes.

powerplant.q: On a field trip, Maya sees a big building with spinning turbines and many power lines leaving it. What is she visiting?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "A power plant". Turbines and power lines are signs of a place that makes electricity.

powerplant.q: How does electricity get from a power plant to your house?
powerplant.hint: The answer is "Through power lines". The grid of power lines transfers electricity to homes.

options: How well something uses energy to do a task
efficiency.hint: The answer is "How well something uses energy to do a task". Efficiency tells how well energy is used to do a job.

efficiency.q: Fill in the blank: An efficient device wastes ____ energy.
efficiency.hint: The answer is "less". Efficient devices waste less energy, like less wasted heat.

options: An efficient device wastes the most heat
Efficiency means how loud a device is
An efficient device wastes less energy
efficiency.hint: The answer is "An efficient device wastes less energy". Being efficient means less energy is wasted.

efficiency.q: Fill in the blank: Efficiency is how ____ something uses energy to do a task.
efficiency.hint: The answer is "well". Efficiency is about how well energy is used.

efficiency.q: Which word means "how well something uses energy to do a task"?
efficiency.hint: The answer is "Efficiency". That is the meaning of efficiency.

efficiency.q: Which light bulb is an example of an efficient bulb?
options: An old bulb too hot to touch
A bulb that turns most energy into heat
An LED bulb that stays cool
efficiency.hint: The answer is "An LED bulb that stays cool". An LED wastes less energy as heat, so it is efficient.

efficiency.q: Which is an example of wasting energy?
efficiency.hint: The answer is "Leaving the fridge door open". An open fridge door lets cold out, so it wastes energy.

efficiency.q: Which group lists only efficient choices?
options: Old hot bulbs and drafty windows
LED bulbs and a well-sealed fridge
An open fridge and a hot old bulb
efficiency.hint: The answer is "LED bulbs and a well-sealed fridge". Both of those waste less energy.

efficiency.q: Which item belongs in the "wastes lots of heat" group?
options: A charger that gets very hot
A solar calculator that stays cool
efficiency.hint: The answer is "A charger that gets very hot". A very hot charger is losing lots of energy as wasted heat.

efficiency.q: Which pot uses the stove's heat more efficiently?
options: A pot with holes in it
efficiency.hint: The answer is "A pot with a lid". A lid keeps heat in, so less energy is wasted.

efficiency.q: Two bulbs give the same light. Bulb A gets very hot. Bulb B stays cool. Which is more efficient?
efficiency.hint: The answer is "Bulb B". Bulb B wastes less energy as heat.

efficiency.q: Why can efficient devices help a family pay less for electricity?
efficiency.hint: The answer is "They waste less energy". Less wasted energy means less electricity is needed.

efficiency.q: Leo's phone charger feels warm while charging. Where did that warmth come from?
options: Some energy was wasted as heat
The phone sent cold into it
efficiency.hint: The answer is "Some energy was wasted as heat". Energy is never made from nothing; some of it always becomes heat.

efficiency.q: At the science fair, Sam puts the same new batteries in two flashlights with the same brightness. X shines 5 hours and Y shines 2 hours. Which is more efficient?
efficiency.hint: The answer is "Flashlight X". X did the same job longer with the same energy, so it wastes less.

efficiency.q: Your family wants to waste less energy lighting the house. What would you use?
options: More lamps left on all night
efficiency.hint: The answer is "LED bulbs". LED bulbs waste less energy as heat.

options: To move something from one place to another
transfer.hint: The answer is "To move something from one place to another". Transfer means moving something from one place to another.

options: From cooler things to warmer things
From warmer things to cooler things
transfer.hint: The answer is "From warmer things to cooler things". Heat always flows from warm to cool.

options: Heat moves from cold things to hot things
The grid transfers electricity to homes
transfer.hint: The answer is "The grid transfers electricity to homes". Power lines in the grid move electricity to homes.

transfer.q: Fill in the blank: To transfer is to ____ something from one place to another.
transfer.hint: The answer is "move". Transfer means to move.

transfer.q: Which word means "to move something from one place to another"?
transfer.hint: The answer is "Transfer". That is the meaning of transfer.

transfer.q: Which is an example of heat transfer?
options: A ball sits still on the floor
A book rests on a shelf
A mug of hot cocoa warms your cold hands
transfer.hint: The answer is "A mug of hot cocoa warms your cold hands". Heat moves from the warm mug to your cooler hands.

transfer.q: Which is an example of electricity being transferred?
options: A pillow sits on a bed
Power lines carry electricity to a school
A crayon lies in a box
transfer.hint: The answer is "Power lines carry electricity to a school". Power lines move electricity from place to place.

transfer.q: Which is NOT an example of transfer?
options: A toy sits still in a box all day
An ice cube melts in your warm hand
A metal spoon warms up in hot soup
transfer.hint: The answer is "A toy sits still in a box all day". Nothing is moving from one place to another with the still toy.

transfer.q: Which item belongs in the "transfers electricity" group?
transfer.hint: The answer is "A copper wire". Metal wires carry electricity; rubber and wood are insulators.

transfer.q: Which is an example of a moving object transferring energy?
options: A bowling ball knocks over pins
A ball resting on a shelf
transfer.hint: The answer is "A bowling ball knocks over pins". The rolling ball moves its energy to the pins.

transfer.q: You put a cold metal spoon in hot soup. What happens?
options: Heat moves from the soup to the spoon
Cold moves from the spoon to the soup
transfer.hint: The answer is "Heat moves from the soup to the spoon". Heat flows from the warmer soup to the cooler spoon.

transfer.q: Why do power lines connect a power plant to homes?
options: To transfer electricity to the homes
To store water for the town
transfer.hint: The answer is "To transfer electricity to the homes". The grid moves electricity from the power plant to homes.

transfer.q: A warm can of juice goes into a cooler full of ice. Predict what happens.
options: The ice gets colder from the juice
The juice cools as heat moves to the ice
transfer.hint: The answer is "The juice cools as heat moves to the ice". Heat flows from the warmer juice to the cooler ice.

transfer.q: Mia wants to send electricity from a battery to a small bulb. What should she use?
transfer.hint: The answer is "A metal wire". Metal wires transfer electricity; plastic and string do not.

transfer.q: On the playground, Ben pushes a swing with his friend on it. What does Ben transfer to the swing?
transfer.hint: The answer is "Energy that makes it move". Ben's push moves energy into the swing so it moves.

options: What comes out of a device
What goes into a system or device
input.hint: The answer is "What goes into a system or device". Input is what goes into a system or device.
The answer is "Electrical energy". A lamp takes in electrical energy.

options: A device needs an input to work
A device makes energy from nothing
Input means the device is broken
input.hint: The answer is "A device needs an input to work". Devices need energy going in before they can do a job.

input.q: Fill in the blank: An input is what goes ____ a system or device.
input.hint: The answer is "into". Input is what goes into a device.

input.q: Which word means "what goes into a system or device"?
input.hint: The answer is "Input". That is the meaning of input.

input.q: For a toaster, which is the energy input?
input.hint: The answer is "Electrical energy from the outlet". The toaster takes in electricity; heat and sound come out.

input.q: When you plug in a radio, what is its energy input?
input.hint: The answer is "Electrical energy". The radio takes in electricity and gives off sound.

input.q: Which is an example of an input?
options: Gas going into a car's tank
Smoke coming out of a car's tailpipe
input.hint: The answer is "Gas going into a car's tank". Gas goes into the car, so it is an input.

input.q: For a solar calculator, which is the energy input?
options: Electrical energy from a wall outlet
input.hint: The answer is "Light energy". A solar calculator takes in light.

input.q: Which belongs on the "inputs" list for a kid riding a bike?
options: Chemical energy from food the rider ate
input.hint: The answer is "Chemical energy from food the rider ate". Food energy goes into the rider to pedal the bike.

input.q: Zoe's lamp will not turn on. She sees it is unplugged. What input is missing?
input.hint: The answer is "Electrical energy". A lamp's input is electrical energy from the outlet.

input.q: Tom turns the key on a wind-up toy car. What is the input?
options: The car rolling across the floor
input.hint: The answer is "The twisting from his hand". Tom's twisting goes into the toy; rolling and clicking come out.

input.q: Lily's science fair project uses a solar panel to light a small bulb. What is the solar panel's input?
input.hint: The answer is "Sunlight". The solar panel takes in sunlight.

input.q: A blender needs an input to spin. What would you do to give it its input?
input.hint: The answer is "Plug it into an outlet". A blender's input is electrical energy from the outlet.

input.q: Predict: What happens if you take away a device's input?
input.hint: The answer is "It stops working". Without energy going in, the device cannot do its job.

options: What comes out of a system or device
output.hint: The answer is "What comes out of a system or device". Output is what comes out of a system or device.
The answer is "Light and heat". A lamp gives off light and heat.

options: Output comes out after a device gets input
Output always goes in before input
A device has outputs but never inputs
output.hint: The answer is "Output comes out after a device gets input". Energy goes in as input and comes out as output.

output.q: Fill in the blank: An output is what comes ____ a system or device.
output.hint: The answer is "out of". Output is what comes out of a device.

output.q: Which word means "what comes out of a system or device"?
output.hint: The answer is "Output". That is the meaning of output.

output.q: For a speaker, which is the main useful output?
output.hint: The answer is "Sound energy". A speaker gives off sound.

output.q: Which is an output of a toaster?
output.hint: The answer is "Heat that browns the bread". Heat comes out of the toaster; electricity goes in.

output.q: Which is NOT an output of a TV?
output.hint: The answer is "Electrical energy from the outlet". Electricity goes into the TV, so it is an input.

output.q: Which belongs on the "outputs" list for a car?
output.hint: The answer is "Exhaust from the tailpipe". Exhaust comes out of the car.

output.q: For an electric fan, which is an output?
output.hint: The answer is "Moving air". The fan's blades move air; electricity is the input.

output.q: You touch a lamp that has been on for an hour and it feels warm. Why?
options: Heat is one of its outputs
output.hint: The answer is "Heat is one of its outputs". A lamp's outputs are light and heat.

output.q: Ana plucks a string on her guitar. What is the output?
output.hint: The answer is "Sound". A plucked guitar string vibrates and makes sound.

output.q: Dad cooks soup on an electric stove. What output cooks the food?
output.hint: The answer is "Heat". The stove takes in electricity and gives off heat.

output.q: You turn on a blender with fruit inside. What output chops the fruit?
output.hint: The answer is "Motion of the spinning blades". The blender turns electricity into motion that chops.

output.q: In class, Kai builds a circuit with a battery and a buzzer. What output tells him it works?
output.hint: The answer is "A buzzing sound". A buzzer's output is sound.

argument.q: What is an argument in science?
options: Using evidence to explain why a claim is best
argument.hint: The answer is "Using evidence to explain why a claim is best". A science argument uses evidence to show a claim is best.

argument.q: In a science argument, what do you use to show your claim is best?
argument.hint: The answer is "Evidence". Arguments use evidence to explain why a claim is best.

options: A science argument connects a claim with evidence
A science argument is an angry fight
A science argument never has a claim
argument.hint: The answer is "A science argument connects a claim with evidence". An argument explains a claim using evidence.

argument.q: Fill in the blank: An argument uses evidence to explain ____ an idea (claim) is best.
argument.hint: The answer is "why". An argument explains why a claim is best.

argument.q: Which word means "using evidence to explain why a claim is best"?
argument.hint: The answer is "Argument". That is the meaning of argument.

argument.q: Which is an example of a science argument?
options: Metal is best because I like it
Metal conducts heat well because our metal spoon got hot fastest
Metal is best, and that is all
argument.hint: The answer is "Metal conducts heat well because our metal spoon got hot fastest". It gives evidence from a test to explain the claim.

argument.q: Which is NOT a science argument?
options: It is true because I said so
The LED is more efficient because it stayed cooler in our test
Rubber is an insulator because the bulb stayed off with it
argument.hint: The answer is "It is true because I said so". Saying so is not evidence.

argument.q: Which pair shows the parts of a science argument?
argument.hint: The answer is "A claim and evidence". An argument uses evidence to support a claim.

argument.q: Which sentence belongs in an argument about which ball bounces highest?
options: The red ball is my favorite
The red ball bounced 50 cm and the blue ball 30 cm
argument.hint: The answer is "The red ball bounced 50 cm and the blue ball 30 cm". Measurements are evidence that support the claim.

argument.q: Which is an example of making an argument in class?
options: Showing your test data to explain your answer
argument.hint: The answer is "Showing your test data to explain your answer". Using data to explain your answer is an argument.

argument.q: Jada claims a covered pot of water heats faster. What should she do to make an argument?
options: Ask everyone to vote without testing
Show test results that support her claim
argument.hint: The answer is "Show test results that support her claim". Arguments use evidence, like test results.

argument.q: Two kids disagree about which bulb is more efficient. What is the best way to settle it?
options: Use evidence from a fair test
argument.hint: The answer is "Use evidence from a fair test". Evidence shows which claim is best.

argument.q: At the science fair, Omar argues that sound travels fastest through solids. What would make his argument strongest?
options: Data showing sound arrived fastest through the solid
argument.hint: The answer is "Data showing sound arrived fastest through the solid". Data is evidence that supports his claim.

argument.q: Ella says black shirts get hotter in the sun. Her teacher asks, "Why do you think so?" What should Ella give?
argument.hint: The answer is "Evidence, like thermometer readings". An argument explains a claim with evidence.

options: To show with evidence which idea is best
argument.hint: The answer is "To show with evidence which idea is best". Arguments use evidence to explain why a claim is best.

options: An answer or statement you believe is correct
claim.hint: The answer is "An answer or statement you believe is correct". A claim is a statement you believe is correct.

options: A claim should be supported by evidence
A claim must always be a question
A claim is a kind of energy
claim.hint: The answer is "A claim should be supported by evidence". Evidence is used to support a claim.

claim.q: Fill in the blank: A claim is an answer or statement that you ____ is correct.
claim.hint: The answer is "believe". A claim is what you believe is correct.

claim.q: Which word means "an answer or statement you believe is correct"?
claim.hint: The answer is "Claim". That is the meaning of claim.

claim.q: Which question does a claim answer?
options: What do you think is correct?
How long did the test take?
claim.hint: The answer is "What do you think is correct?". A claim is your answer that you believe is correct.

claim.q: Which of these is a claim?
claim.hint: The answer is "Rubber is an electrical insulator.". A claim is a statement, not a question or a command.

claim.q: Which of these is NOT a claim?
options: Wood is a bad heat conductor.
claim.hint: The answer is "What color is the sky?". A question is not a statement you believe is correct.

claim.q: Which part of a science fair poster is the claim?
claim.hint: The answer is "Sound travels fastest through solids". That is the statement the student believes is correct.

options: How tall is it? Where is it?
Plants need light. Ice melts in the sun.
claim.hint: The answer is "Plants need light. Ice melts in the sun.". Those are statements someone believes are correct.

claim.q: Mia says, "I think the LED bulb is more efficient." What is this?
claim.hint: The answer is "A claim". Mia states what she believes, with no data yet.

claim.q: Leo's teacher asks for his claim about which ball bounces highest. What should he say?
options: I think the rubber ball bounces highest
claim.hint: The answer is "I think the rubber ball bounces highest". A claim is the answer he believes is correct.

claim.q: Ava claims dark shirts get warmer in the sun. What should she do next to support it?
options: Turn her claim into a question
claim.hint: The answer is "Collect evidence by testing". Evidence supports a claim.

claim.q: Two students make different claims about which cup keeps cocoa warm longer. How can they find out which is best?
options: Test both cups and compare evidence
claim.hint: The answer is "Test both cups and compare evidence". Evidence shows which claim is best.

claim.q: Sam's test results show his claim was wrong. What should he do?
options: Change his claim to match the evidence
claim.hint: The answer is "Change his claim to match the evidence". A good claim must agree with the evidence.

claim.q: Nora's question is "Does water conduct electricity?" Which claim agrees with the study guide?
options: Water is an insulator like rubber
claim.hint: The answer is "Water is an electrical conductor". The study guide says water is a strong conductor of electricity.

options: Information or facts that support a claim
evidence.hint: The answer is "Information or facts that support a claim". Evidence is information or facts that support a claim.

evidence.q: What does evidence do for a claim?
evidence.hint: The answer is "Supports it". Evidence supports an answer or claim.

options: Evidence is the same as a guess
evidence.hint: The answer is "Test results can be evidence". Facts from tests are information that support a claim.

evidence.q: Fill in the blank: Evidence is information or facts that ____ an answer or claim.
evidence.hint: The answer is "support". Evidence supports a claim.

evidence.q: Which word means "information or facts that support a claim"?
evidence.hint: The answer is "Evidence". That is the meaning of evidence.

options: I hope it is hot today
evidence.hint: The answer is "The thermometer read 30 degrees". A measurement is a fact that can support a claim.

evidence.q: Which of these is NOT evidence?
options: I just feel like it is true
Our chart shows the LED stayed cooler
evidence.hint: The answer is "I just feel like it is true". A feeling is not a fact.

evidence.q: Which group lists only kinds of evidence?
evidence.hint: The answer is "Measurements, observations, test results". These are all facts and information.

evidence.q: Claim: "Metal is a good heat conductor." Which is evidence for it?
options: A metal spoon in hot cocoa got hot quickly
evidence.hint: The answer is "A metal spoon in hot cocoa got hot quickly". That fact shows metal moves heat well.

evidence.q: Which item belongs in a science evidence notebook?
evidence.hint: The answer is "A table of measured temperatures". Measurements are evidence.

evidence.q: Kim claims rubber is an electrical insulator. Which evidence supports her claim?
options: The bulb did not light with rubber in the circuit
evidence.hint: The answer is "The bulb did not light with rubber in the circuit". The bulb staying off shows rubber blocks electricity.

evidence.q: Jake claims black paper heats up more in sunlight than white paper. What should he collect?
evidence.hint: The answer is "Temperature readings under each paper". Temperature readings are evidence for his claim.

evidence.q: Your friend says, "Trust me, glass conducts electricity." What should you ask for?
evidence.hint: The answer is "Evidence". Claims need evidence; and glass is really an insulator.

evidence.q: A team's evidence shows a wooden spoon stayed cool in hot water. What claim does it support?
options: Wood is a great heat conductor
Wood is a bad heat conductor
evidence.hint: The answer is "Wood is a bad heat conductor". Wood is a bad heat conductor, so the spoon stayed cool.

evidence.q: Ali's bulb lit up when pencil graphite was in the circuit. What claim does this evidence support?
evidence.hint: The answer is "Graphite is a good conductor". Graphite is a good conductor, so electricity flowed.
